Acute COPD exacerbation / infection.short_description: A sudden worsening of COPD symptoms such as breathlessness, cough, wheezing or increased mucus. Respiratory infections can sometimes trigger a flare-up.

Acute laryngitis.short_description: Short-term inflammation of the voice box and vocal cords that may cause hoarseness, a weak voice, sore throat or cough.

Acute pulmonary edema.display_name: Sudden Fluid Build-Up in the Lungs
Acute pulmonary edema.short_description: A sudden build-up of fluid inside the lungs that can make breathing very difficult and requires prompt medical assessment.

Acute rhinosinusitis.short_description: Short-term inflammation of the nose and sinuses that may cause a blocked or runny nose, facial pressure, headache and nasal discharge.

Allergic sinusitis.short_description: Inflammation of the nose and sinus areas linked to allergies, which may cause congestion, nasal symptoms and facial pressure.

Bronchiectasis.short_description: A long-term condition where damaged airways become widened and can trap mucus, leading to persistent cough and repeated chest infections.

Bronchiolitis.short_description: Inflammation of the small airways in the lungs, often caused by a viral infection and commonly affecting infants and young children.

Bronchitis.short_description: Inflammation of the main airways leading to the lungs, commonly causing cough and sometimes increased mucus.

Bronchospasm / acute asthma exacerbation.short_description: A sudden narrowing of the airways that may cause wheezing, coughing, chest tightness and shortness of breath.

Chronic rhinosinusitis.short_description: Long-lasting inflammation of the nose and sinuses that may cause ongoing congestion, facial pressure, nasal discharge or reduced sense of smell.

Croup.short_description: An upper-airway illness, most common in young children, that can cause swelling around the vocal cords, a barking cough, hoarseness and noisy breathing.

Epiglottitis.short_description: Inflammation and swelling of the tissue protecting the windpipe. It can interfere with breathing and can become a medical emergency.

Influenza.short_description: A contagious viral respiratory infection that can cause fever, body aches, tiredness, headache, cough and other respiratory symptoms.

Larygospasm.short_description: A sudden involuntary tightening of the vocal cords that can temporarily make it difficult to breathe or speak.

Pneumonia.short_description: An infection of the lungs that may cause cough, fever or chills, chest discomfort and shortness of breath.

Pulmonary neoplasm.short_description: An abnormal growth of cells in lung tissue. Lung growths require proper medical assessment to determine their type and significance.

Spontaneous pneumothorax.short_description: A condition where air collects around a lung and causes part or all of the lung to collapse, sometimes without an obvious injury.

Tuberculosis.short_description: An infection caused by tuberculosis bacteria. Active lung TB may cause a long-lasting cough, fever, night sweats, tiredness or weight loss.

URTI.short_description: An infection affecting the nose, throat or other upper airways, commonly causing symptoms such as congestion, sore throat and cough.

Viral pharyngitis.short_description: Inflammation of the throat caused by a virus, commonly resulting in soreness, discomfort or pain when swallowing.

Whooping cough.short_description: A highly contagious bacterial respiratory infection that can cause repeated severe coughing fits and may last for several weeks.

COVID-19.short_description: A respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. It may cause fever, cough, sore throat, tiredness, breathing difficulties and other symptoms.

Allergic rhinitis.short_description: An allergic reaction affecting the nose, which may cause sneezing, a runny or blocked nose, itching and watery eyes.
